sections.h2: Who values and bills property tax in Charlotte?
sections.html:
Mecklenburg County's Office of Tax Administration values every parcel in Charlotte and collects the county's tax, and the City of Charlotte's own property tax rides on the same bill. A total bill includes a municipal tax from Charlotte or one of the six county towns, plus county and municipal solid waste fees where they apply. Payments go to the City-County Tax Collector.

The office values parcels, collects property tax and business gross receipts tax, and runs relief programs. Appeals, relief applications and the revaluation all go through the county. City Council's part is the city rate, which it sets in its yearly budget.

You can pay by a toll-free card line at 1-800-994-1026 that answers day and night, by mailed check to a Charlotte post office box, by bank eCheck, or at the counter during weekday office hours. A payment with no 24-digit bill number in the account box is rejected and returned. Cards carry a vendor fee of $3.95 on Visa or Mastercard debit and 2.35 percent (minimum $1.95) on other cards, while eChecks carry none. Payments started from your bank may take as long as four business days to post.

The Mecklenburg County rate is 49.27 cents on each $100 of value for FY2027, unchanged from FY2026. The city rate comes on top of it for property inside Charlotte, and the figure for a given year appears on your bill and in the city budget.

sections.h2: How to contest a Charlotte tax value
sections.html:
Your Formal Appeal Form goes to the county Office of Tax Administration, and the board of equalization and review hears the case. In a normal year the deadline is the board's adjournment date each spring. The only exception is for owners who receive a notice of value change, who may file by the later of adjournment or the last date to appeal on the notice.

  • File by email to the county's appeals address, by mail to Mecklenburg County BER Real Property Appeals, P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at 3205 Freedom Dr, Suite 3500, Charlotte, NC 28208.
  • Back-up documents must arrive with the form or within 45 days of filing it. Anyone other than you or an attorney who speaks for you needs a signed power of attorney.
  • Expect the hearing notice roughly a month before your slot, and send any request to reschedule in writing within ten days of that notice.
  • The board's ruling comes by mail within a month of the hearing. Anyone who still disagrees can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh, within 30 days.

The burden sits with the owner, who must show the tax value substantially exceeds market value. No revaluation-year appeal can be filed before notices of value go out, and the county expects the notices and refreshed online records in early 2027.

Between revaluations, the county keeps the prior value unless a ground in G.S. 105-287(a) applies. Those grounds are clerical or arithmetic mistakes, a misapplied schedule of values, physical changes to the land or buildings, and a change in legal use.

Mecklenburg County runs the state homestead programs from its tax relief page, and its FY2027 budget carries $3.5 million for the county's HOMES program for qualifying homeowners. A Charlotte owner applies to the county for all of them.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the taxable amount drops by $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is more. Owners must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, with income inside the cap, which is $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes $45,000 off the appraised value. The application is Form NCDVA-9, and age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: the portion of the bill above 4 or 5 percent of income is deferred, with the percentage set by where income falls between the cap and $58,200. The deferred amount is a lien and, on a transfer, comes due together with the prior three years.

Income is defined broadly and counts every source except family gifts and inheritances. The county takes Form AV-9 applications until June 1 ahead of the tax year.

Closing clears any balance from your proceeds, since the debt stays with the parcel. The lien arises January 1. A house sold in March therefore already owes that year's tax, though September 1 is months away. Treat that year's amount as a payoff line.

Interest starts after January 5: 2 percent for what is left of January, and three-fourths of a percent for each later month. Long nonpayment lets the county file a court action modeled on mortgage foreclosure, with an auction sale. An owner can redeem ahead of confirmation by paying everything owed. The tax office site also hosts a Delinquent Taxpayer Lists page.

For the deed, the seller (transferor) pays the state excise tax to the Mecklenburg County register of deeds ahead of recording. Your closing attorney can confirm the stamps and filing charges that will show on the settlement statement.

To prepare, ask the Office of Tax Administration for the balance on your 24-digit bill, and check whether a circuit breaker deferral or other relief is on the parcel, since a deferral adds prior years to the payoff. Pass both numbers to the closing attorney before signing a contract. With a cash buyer there is no lender payoff, and the tax just comes out of proceeds at the table.

Charlotte's July 1, 2025 estimate is 964,784 residents, a 10.3 percent gain on 2020. Owners occupy 51.0 percent of homes, which leaves renters with almost half. A typical owned home was valued at $385,700 for 2020-2024.

The 2027 values will draw on four years of sales since 2023. If you list in early 2027, keep an eye out for the notice mailing. The new assessment shapes later tax bills, and a buyer may ask about it.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in Charlotte?
faqs.a: The county levy is 49.27 cents on each $100 of value, unchanged for FY2027. Charlotte adds its own city rate for property inside the city, set by City Council each year. Your bill shows both, along with any solid waste fee.

faqs.q: When is the next Charlotte revaluation?
faqs.a: The next one lands in 2027. Mecklenburg now revalues on a four-year cycle, and 2023 was the last one. Expect notices and refreshed online records in early 2027. An informal review can be requested within 30 days of the notice date.

faqs.q: How do I pay a Charlotte property tax bill?
faqs.a: Use the card line at 1-800-994-1026, send an eCheck, mail a check to the City-County Tax Collector, or visit during weekday hours. Include the 24-digit bill number, since a payment without it is returned. Cards bring a vendor fee.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Charlotte property value after the deadline?
faqs.a: Generally no. Each spring the board of equalization and review adjourns, and that date is the cutoff unless a notice of value change gave you a later one. The next broad opening follows the 2027 revaluation notices.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid Charlotte property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Closing takes it from your proceeds, with interest added once the bill is past January 5. The lien has attached to the parcel since January 1 of the tax year. Get the balance from the Mecklenburg Office of Tax Administration before you sign a contract.
